name: THAT LOOKS FAMILIAR
notes: Facts all verified (Sistine 1508-12, Arc's unknown soldier, 'Three Coins' 1954, 887 moai/Roggeveen); all five clues ran 101-117 chars, far past the easy register, so every row was trimmed to 87-95.

name: THE VACATION SLIDESHOW
notes: Adams-first-resident, King Kong 1933, State House steeple, 1836 Alamo and the 605-ft 1962 Space Needle all check out; US-landmark theme echoes e1-century's WISH YOU WERE HERE but shares no answers.

name: THE PRIDE OF THE STATE
notes: $200 and $400 handed over 'Lone Star State' and 'Sunshine State' — a giveaway that also duplicated the sibling category NICKNAME THAT STATE's whole gimmick; both rewritten to non-nickname cues (lower-48 size, southeastern peninsula).

name: NICKNAME THAT STATE
notes: Golden/Lincoln/Buckeye/Big Sky/Beehive all correct and Montana is unambiguously Wyoming's northern neighbor; textbook gentle ladder.

name: CAPITALS OF THE OLD WORLD
notes: Verified Brandenburg Gate completed 1791; Parthenon, Prado, Liffey/'Ulysses' and the Little Mermaid all solid, each capital unambiguous.

name: CAPITALS FAR FROM HOME
notes: All five accurate and evergreen; the $1000 Bangkok row names Thailand outright, making it plain recall rather than a hook, but it lands as a gentle finisher.

name: WATER, WATER EVERYWHERE
notes: Edmund Fitzgerald 1975 on Superior (largest NA freshwater lake), Rio Grande as the entire TX-Mexico border and the 1869 Suez opening all check out; two clues run ~100 chars.

name: THE HILLS ARE ALIVE
notes: Rockies' New Mexico-to-Canada span, Hemingway's Kilimanjaro title, Disneyland's 1959 Matterhorn bobsleds and the Urals as the Europe-Asia line all verified.

name: THE COUNTRY IT COMES FROM
notes: $1000 'sheep outnumber people in this Pacific home of lamb and wool' fit Australia as well as New Zealand — reworded to the North and South Islands to force one answer; other four verified.

name: THE SOUVENIR SHELF
notes: Sombrero, kilt, klompen/tulips, matryoshka and Waterford/Aran all accurate and evergreen; ladder is gentle to the point of flat, but every row is a warm memory.

name: WONDERFUL, WONDERFUL
notes: $1000 Temple of Artemis was the file's one specialist ask (and collides with the Temple of Diana naming) — replaced with the Halicarnassus tomb that gave English 'mausoleum', a reasoning path a casual player can walk; $200 also trimmed from 106 chars.

name: KNOW IT BY ITS FLAG
notes: Verified Greece's nine stripes and Israel's two blue bars; Turkey row's 'Europe and Asia' correctly rules out Tunisia's similar flag; all described in words, no image dependency.
